title: Design a URL Shortener (TinyURL)
content:
# System Design: URL Shortener (TinyURL / Bitly)

---

## 1. Requirements & Scale Estimation
- **Functional:** 
  - Generate a unique short URL (e.g. `https://tiny.url/aZ8k9Q`) given a long URL.
  - Redirect short URLs to the original destination with 301/302 HTTP redirects.
  - Custom aliases and analytics (click counts).
- **Scale:** 100M new URLs created/month, 10B redirects/month (100:1 read-to-write ratio).
- **Storage:** Base62 encoding (`[a-zA-Z0-9]`). With 7 characters, Base62 provides $62^7 \approx 3.5 \text{ Trillion}$ unique combinations.

---

## 2. Architecture Diagram

```
Client ──> DNS / CDN (Cloudflare) ──> Load Balancer (Nginx)
                                              │
                     ┌────────────────────────┴────────────────────────┐
                     ▼                                                 ▼
             Write Service (POST /shorten)                    Read Service (GET /:hash)
                     │                                                 │
       ┌─────────────┴─────────────┐                                   ▼
       ▼                           ▼                             Redis Cache (Hot URLs)
Token Range Service         PostgreSQL / Cassandra                     │ (Cache Miss)
 (Zookeeper KGS)             (Primary DB Cluster) ◄────────────────────┘
```

---

## 3. Core Technical Decisions
- **Unique Hash Generation:** Use a **Key Generation Service (KGS)** with pre-allocated numeric ranges via Zookeeper or Redis `INCR` mapped to Base62.
- **Redirect Status:** 
  - `301 Moved Permanently`: Browser caches redirect locally (faster, but loses real-time click analytics).
  - `302 Found`: Browser requests redirect from server every time (enables accurate click tracking).

title: Design a Real-Time Chat Application (WhatsApp/Slack)
content:
# System Design: Real-Time Chat Application

---

## 1. Core Requirements
- 1-on-1 direct messaging and group chats (up to 1,000 members).
- Real-time delivery with online/offline presence tracking and read receipts.
- Message persistence and end-to-end encryption.

---

## 2. Architecture & Data Flow

```
User A (WebSocket) ──> Gateway / WS Server A ──> Redis Pub/Sub / Kafka ──> WS Server B ──> User B (WebSocket)
                              │
                              ▼
                     Cassandra / ScyllaDB (Message History)
```

---

## 3. Key Components:
- **Transport Protocol:** Persistent bi-directional **WebSockets** for active connections; fallback to Push Notifications (APNs / FCM) for offline users.
- **Message Storage:** Wide-column NoSQL (**Apache Cassandra / ScyllaDB**) partitioned by `chat_id` with `message_id` clustering key for high-throughput append writes and fast range queries.
- **Presence Engine:** Redis Key-Value with heartbeat TTL (every 30s) to detect active/idle connections.

title: Design an API Rate Limiter
content:
# System Design: Distributed API Rate Limiter

---

## 1. Goals & SLA
- Limit requests per client (by API Key or IP) with low latency overhead (< 2ms).
- Distributed accuracy across multiple multi-region API Gateway nodes.

---

## 2. Sliding Window Log Algorithm with Redis & Lua Scripting

```lua
-- atomic_rate_limit.lua
local key = KEYS[1]
local now = tonumber(ARGV[1])
local window = tonumber(ARGV[2])
local limit = tonumber(ARGV[3])
local clearBefore = now - window

-- 1. Remove expired timestamps
redis.call('ZREMRANGEBYSCORE', key, 0, clearBefore)

-- 2. Count requests in current window
local currentRequests = redis.call('ZCARD', key)

if currentRequests < limit then
  -- 3. Record new timestamp
  redis.call('ZADD', key, now, now)
  redis.call('EXPIRE', key, window / 1000)
  return 1 -- Allowed
else
  return 0 -- Rejected (429 Too Many Requests)
end
```
